Maria Chen: Heads-up — we need a formal apples-to-apples benchmarking protocol for continuous-batching experiments. Current noise between replay vs synth makes comparisons fuzzy.
Jon Patel: +1. Can you sketch constraints? e.g., same kernel, same kvcache state, same seq-len dist?
Maria Chen: Exactly. Proposal: 1) fixed kernel binary (no dynamic kernel switching), 2) three kv cache states: cold, warm, steady, 3) match seq-len and temperature distributions from production 24h slice.
Liam O'Neill: For (2) how do we define warm vs steady?
Maria Chen: Warm = cache populated from a short warmup replay (30m of traffic), steady = long-run (>6h) with steady hit rates. Cold = clean VM + empty cache.
Sasha K: We should also control batching knobs: batch_size_cap, max_delay_ms, batch_priority policy. Document exact values.
Jon Patel: +1. My suggested baseline knobs: batch_size_cap=64, max_delay_ms=8, priority=FIFO. Then test caps {16,32,64,128} and delays {2,4,8,16}.
perf-bot: perf-bot: auto-run queued: benchmark-job/1776004321 started (replay harness, kernel v2.7.1, dataset=prod-2026-02-10).
Maria Chen: One more apples-to-apples rule: synthetic traffic generators must support the same concurrency/thinktime distribution as replay. No synthetic that always fills full batches instantly.
Liam O'Neill: Agree. For synthetic we can parametrize inter-arrival using Pareto + Poisson mix. I’ll add the script and seed it for determinism.
Sasha K: Also add tenant-mix experiments: 1 heavy tenant (80qps) + 10 small ones (2-5qps) to measure fairness under batch caps.
Jon Patel: And a headroom test: push 1.5x the expected qps to see graceful degradation and fallback to smaller kernel/FP16 variant.
Maria Chen: Can we capture per-tenant metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/s, batch fill ratio, kv hit rate? Need those in the dashboard export.
infra-bot: infra-bot: perf-metrics exporter enabled for run 1776004321. Grafana link: https://grafana.internal/r/bench/1776004321
perf-bot: perf-bot: run complete. Brief results below (summary):
  - baseline (cap=64, delay=8ms, warm cache): p50=38ms, p95=112ms, tps=4200 tokens/s, avg batch fill=44
  - cap=16: p50=31ms, p95=98ms, tps=2700 tokens/s, avg batch fill=12 (higher queuing short-delay)
  - cap=128: p50=45ms, p95=140ms, tps=4800 tokens/s, avg batch fill=62
  - cold cache baseline: p95 jumps to 280ms, kv hit rate drops to 18%
  - tenant-mix: heavy tenant saw p95 inflation +22% vs solo; small tenants saw p95 +60% under cap=128; cap=32 improved fairness (small tenants p95 down by ~30%)
Liam O'Neill: Interesting that cap=128 gives best throughput but worst small-tenant fairness. That matches queueing intuition.
Jon Patel: That suggests a recommended default cap=64 but per-tenant cap override to protect small tenants. Maybe a floor of 32 for tenant-specific caps.
Sasha K: We also observed a perf regression when switching to kernel v2.8.0-alpha: p95 +18% even with same batch knobs. Need kernel profiler traces.
Maria Chen: Who owns kernel change? @Liam can you run nvprof/trace on v2.8 and extract timeline of matmul vs softmax? Put flamegraphs in the run artifact.
Liam O'Neill: On it. If regression repros, we’ll bisect commits and try falling back to earlier kernel selection heuristic (prefer fast-softmax path for short seq).
perf-bot: perf-bot: attached trace: s3://perf-artifacts/1776004321/v2.8-trace.tar.gz
Jon Patel: For loadtest reproducibility — record exact seed, workload descriptor, and binary sha. Also store the orchestrator config (node counts, CUDA visible devices).
Maria Chen: Agreed. Add to protocol checklist: commit_sha, kernel_sha, cfg.json, seed, replay-window (start/end), kv prewarm script hash.
Sasha K: On fairness policy, propose test matrix: caps {32,64,128}, delays {4,8}, tenant priority {equal, weighted (heavy=3x)}. Report: p50/p95 per tenant + tail fairness metric (95th-percentile ratio heavy/small).
Jon Patel: Good. Also include a microburst probe: 100ms spike of 10x qps to measure queue spill and drop rates.
Maria Chen: Action items: Liam run v2.8 profiler (assigned), Jon update benchmark harness to emit deterministic seeds and cfg (assigned), Sasha assemble fairness matrix and dashboards (assigned). We’ll reconvene after next run.
Liam O'Neill: Starting profiler now, ETA ~45m.
perf-bot: perf-bot: scheduled follow-up run 1776005600 for full fairness matrix.
Maria Chen: Thanks team. Keep notes concise in the ticket (TKT-1279) and link runs to the PR that changes kernel heuristics. :thumbsup:
Sasha K: Noted. I’ll push a draft doc for the protocol by EOD.
